title: PRD: Minimal Interop Endpoint Bundle (chat / gen / embeddings / rerank) + Launch Criteria
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a tightly scoped "minimal interop endpoint" bundle that exposes a single, opinionated hosted API experience covering: chat (conversational), generation/completions, embeddings, and rerank. The goal is a low-friction entry point for developers who need consistent defaults, predictable semantics across modalities, and a small launch surface that maps to existing Redwood runtime capabilities.
goals: Provide a single onboarding endpoint bundle that covers the 4 common primitives with consistent request/response shapes and predictable defaults
Minimize fragmentation by standardizing parameter names and fallback behavior across modalities
Ship a production-ready launch with telemetry, SLOs, and an ops-runbook for early customers
Keep scope intentionally small to accelerate launch: no multi-model orchestration in v1, no advanced billing tiers
non_goals: Supporting multi-turn conversational session storage managed by the customer in v1 (we will provide stateless defaults)
Advanced per-token billing experiments or complex pricing packaging in the initial launch
Full parity with every existing hosted endpoint variation (this is a curated minimal bundle)
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want a single quickstart example that covers chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank so I can prototype an MVP with one integration
As an ML engineer, I want predictable default temperature/beam settings mapped across modalities so model behavior is easier to evaluate
As an SRE, I need clear SLOs and fallback policies documented so we can maintain reliability during the canary
scope: API surface: a bundled set of endpoints with harmonized parameter names (prompt -> input, max_tokens -> length_cap, temperature -> randomness) and explicit modality tag

Default runtime behavior: KV prefix caching enabled for chat and completions where beneficial; embeddings use batched vectorization path; rerank uses lightweight similarity reranker backed by embeddings
Docs: quickstart guide, example SDK snippets (Python/JS), and an FAQ mapping old endpoint names to bundle parameters
Operational: canary rollout plan, cost telemetry dashboard, runbook for model fallback and capacity pressure
scope_changes: 2025-06-12: Reduced initial model catalog to 3 curated variants (small/medium/large) instead of open catalog to shorten onboarding for compliance review
2025-06-14: Removed session-managed KV store from v1; implement stateless prefix caching and document migration path
2025-06-16: Defanged advanced function-calling in the chat modality for v1 (support only structured response hints) to reduce safety surface
technical_constraints: Must reuse existing runtime kernel selection — no new kernel development in this sprint
Target p95 latency: chat/completions <= 220ms for small model under typical canary load; embeddings p95 <= 180ms for batched calls
Quota and rate-limits must honor existing per-account throttles; do not add new global rate-limit variables in v1
Audit logs and KMS integration must be compatible with Private customers but additive (no migration required)
acceptance_criteria: API contracts published and validated by SDK smoke tests (Python/JS) with example apps in repo
End-to-end canary completed on dedicated test org with at least 10% of internal traffic and zero P0 incidents for 72h
Telemetry: per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, error-rate alerts created and firing thresholds documented
Safety: basic content-filtering integration enabled for generation endpoints; documented failure modes and fallback to lower-cost model
Docs: Quickstart + migration mapping document published in Confluence and linked in product website
Compliance: security review completed and findings remediated (security_review_required = true)
launch_checklist: Finalize API parameter mapping and publish OpenAPI contract
Merge SDK examples and release patch in Python and JS packages
Create runtime canary configuration and schedule 72h internal canary window
Provision telemetry dashboards: per-route cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, token throughput
Coordinate PM/Eng/DevRel announcement and customer outreach list
Confirm billing path: map bundle usage to existing hosted usage invoices
Prepare rollback playbook: immediate model downgrade and regional traffic cutover steps
Run security checklist: KMS keys verified, audit logging enabled, SSO access gated for launch cohort
Prepare post-launch evaluation probes and quality regression prompts (eval set)
rollout_plan: Week 0 (canary): internal-only canary with 5 internal teams and 10% internal traffic for 72 hours
Week 1 (private beta): invite 8 pilot customers (mix of startups and enterprise) with close SLAs and weekly syncs
Week 3 (wider beta): open self-serve with feature flag enabled for 25% new sign-ups; monitor cost and latency metrics
Week 6 (general availability): GA with docs, pricing mapping, and public announcement if metrics are green
success_metrics: Adoption: 3 pilot customers onboarded and 30 self-serve integrations within 30 days of beta
Reliability: p95 latency targets met in 95% of observation windows during beta
Cost: per-token serving cost within 10% of modeled estimates for the bundle
Quality: no more than 2% of eval prompts showing quality regressions compared to baseline model
